summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would fix technical defects in export laws and allow the Department of Agriculture to recover costs for export services.
The package would align definitions in the Export Inspection and Meat Charges Collection Act 1985 with those in the Export Control Act 1982.
The bill would also amend the Australian Meat and Live-stock Industry Act 1997 to let the department recover costs for quota arrangements run by other countries.
changes: Remedies technical defects in the Export Control Act 1982, Export Inspection and Meat Charges Collection Act 1985, and the Imported Food Control Act 1992.
Aligns definitions in the Export Inspection and Meat Charges Collection Act 1985 with the Export Control Act 1982.
Amends the Australian Meat and Live-stock Industry Act 1997 to enable cost recovery for quota arrangements administered by other countries.
summary.affected: The Department of Agriculture and exporters using its services.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Introduced the second of four export legislation bills, the Export Inspection (Quantity Charge) Amendment Bill, making consequential changes for consistency with the broader reforms without imposing any extra charges.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Introduced the third of four export legislation bills, the Export Inspection (Service Charge) Amendment Bill, making consequential amendments for consistency with the broader reforms without imposing any extra charges.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Introduced the final of four export legislation bills, allowing the department to recover establishment registration charges from exporters of products like cut flowers, dried fruit, nursery stock, nuts, seed, timber and tissue culture without imposing new fees.

speeches.speaker: Joel Fitzgibbon
speeches.brief: Welcomed the Export Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 for standardising cost-recovery definitions across seven statutes, allowing the Department of Agriculture to recover an estimated $1.9 million a year, and moved a second reading amendment noting the Quarantine Act 1908 is over a century old and needs updating per the Beale review.

speeches.speaker: John Cobb
speeches.brief: Argued that AQIS export inspection costs should be made more efficient and contestable, and said Australia does more trade with New Zealand, a country of 4½ million people, than with the nearly quarter of a billion people in Indonesia, calling this imbalance something to redress.

speeches.speaker: Clare O'Neil
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Export Legislation Amendment Bill 2014, cited a Deloitte report estimating growing food exports could add $250 billion to the Australian economy over the next two decades, and noted Labor invested $1.6 billion while in government to minimise biosecurity threats to primary production.

speeches.speaker: Rowan Ramsey
speeches.brief: Argued in support of the Export Legislation Amendment Bill 2014, noting there are 676 registered exporters currently paying registration fees compared with 269 who are not, and cited the New Zealand botulism scare in which French company Danone is suing Fonterra for NZ$492 million in damages.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Summed up the debate on the Export Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 package, said Australia's farm, fish and forest exports were worth more than $41 billion in 2012 to 2013, and noted the Griffith area of his Riverina electorate generates about $800 million a year in wine exports from three-quarters of New South Wales' wine grapes.
